ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the side length of the regular hexagon inscribed in a circle is 6. What is the radius of the circle?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AOB$ is the central angle of a regular hexagon,\\
it follows that $\angle AOB=\frac{1}{6}\times 360^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
and since $OA=OB$,\\
it follows that $\triangle AOB$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
hence $OA=AB=\boxed{6}$,\\
which means the radius of this regular hexagon is 6.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the figure contains a circle circumscribing a regular hexagon, with the bottom chord AB marked as one side and labeled 6; O is shown as the center of the circle. Read from the text that the side length of the regular hexagon is 6. Treat AB as a chord of the circle subtending one-sixth of the full circumference at the center.
